name: DeepTutor
cost: Free (Apache 2.0). You bring your own model provider
works_with: Any model provider you set up in Settings. Can also consult agents like Claude Code, Codex and others from chat
short: A self-hosted AI tutor with chat, quizzes, research, problem solving and study plans that share one memory of what you know.
what: DeepTutor is a learning workspace you run yourself. It puts tutoring, quiz generation, research, problem solving, visual explanations and mastery practice in one app, with knowledge bases built from your own material. It keeps an editable memory of what you have learned and has a command-line tool that other agents can drive.
who: Students, self-learners and teachers who want an AI tutor on their own machine using their own documents. If you just want a quick chat about a topic, a regular chat app is simpler.
needs: Docker for the one-command trial, or Python 3.11 to 3.14 and Node.js 20 or newer for the PyPI install
An LLM provider, base URL, API key and model. An embedding provider for knowledge bases and a search provider for web search are optional

steps.title: Try it with Docker
steps.text: Then open http://127.0.0.1:3782 and add a model provider in Settings, then Providers. Press Ctrl+C to stop. The named volume keeps your settings for next time.

steps.title: Or install it from PyPI
steps.text: `deeptutor init` asks for ports, your LLM provider and key, and optional embedding and search providers. Keep the terminal open while it runs.
steps.code:
mkdir -p my-deeptutor && cd my-deeptutor
pip install -U "deeptutor[full]"
deeptutor init     # prompts for ports + LLM provider + optional embedding/search
deeptutor start    # starts backend + frontend; keep the terminal open

steps.title: Open the app
steps.text: Go to the URL the terminal prints, by default http://127.0.0.1:3782.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `deeptutor run chat "Explain the Fourier transform"` for a one-turn answer, or `deeptutor chat` for an interactive session.

watch: Your questions and documents go to whichever model provider you configure.
Agents in DeepTutor can read your content workspace folder. Running commands is read-only outside `outputs/`, and copying files elsewhere needs your confirmation.

The README offers a prompt to paste into a coding agent so it installs DeepTutor for you. That agent then clones the dev branch and handles your provider keys, so read the Agent Setup guide first if you go that way.
Upgrading to 1.7.0 has extra steps if the old `deeptutor-cli` package is installed. Back up your data first.
